title: POC cost modeling + benchmark plan - NovaHealth
summary: Customer wants a 6-week POC to validate per-token economics for clinical summarization use case.
Primary success criteria: <10% latency regressions vs current infra, <40% increase in monthly infra cost, and HIPAA-safe data handling with audit logs.
Plan: three benchmark profiles (interactive summarization, async batch ingestion, embeddings for search) with cost/per-token and latency targets.
next_steps: Redwood to share POC runbook and pricing assumptions sheet by 2025-11-07
Customer to provide sample throughput histogram and 14-day request traces by 2025-11-10
Schedule benchmark kickoff (env setup) for week of 2025-11-17
action_items: Jordan Park | Send POC runbook + pricing workbook | 2025-11-07
Ben Carter | Export 14-day request traces and schema | 2025-11-10
Maya Singh | Draft micro-benchmark tests and baseline scripts | 2025-11-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 mins
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood), Priya Rao (CTO - NovaHealth), Ben Carter (MLOps), Sara Lopez (Product)
Shared links: redwood.com/poc-template (deck), /redwood/security/hitrust-brief.pdf, shared spreadsheet: NovaHealth-poc-pricing.xlsx

00:00 Jordan Park: Ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to focus today on the econ and scope for the poc, specifically unit cost expectations and the bench plan, maybe quick round robin on objectives?
00:18 Priya Rao: Hi, priya here — main goal is to prove we can hit production latency for interactive summarization and also not blow up monthly infra spend, we have a budget cap at roughly $30k/mo for inference, that's across the app.
00:30 Ben Carter: Right and to add, the current on-prem service averages 180ms per request (95th) with our trimmed model, and cost is mostly ops and GPU amortization; we need a realistic per-token estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:48 Maya Singh: Great, we'll do three profiles: interactive summarization (short chat-like prompts, 350 tokens avg output), async batch summarization (large docs, 3k tokens), and embeddings for search (dense, mostly encoder forward pass). We'll capture per-token, per-request latencies, and effective throughput under batching.
01:06 Sara Lopez: Also want to see caching behavior — a lot of our traffic repeats patient note prefixes, is KV/prefix caching a realistic knob?
01:18 Luis Ortega: Yeah, Redwood has prefix/KV cache and we can demo savings. Important to model hit rates — we should baseline with 0%, 25%, 50% hit rates.
01:33 Ben Carter: On quantization, we already run int8 for some models; curious how Redwood's quantized variants compare — latency vs quality tradeoffs.
01:44 Jordan Park: We'll include model variant matrix (fp16, int8, int4 candidates) and quality checks using a 1000-query evaluation set you provide. We'll report perplexity proxies and sample-level QA checks so you see regression risk.
02:00 Priya Rao: Success criteria — I want explicit thresholds: (a) 95p latency <= 300ms for interactive, (b) batch throughput >= 1200 tokens/sec sustained for nightly ingest, (c) per-token hosted cost <= $0.0009 for critical models, and (d) audit logs/KMS integration must be demonstrable.
02:21 Maya Singh: Noted. We'll map those to config knobs: batch size, max latency SLO, cache TTLs, routing to dedicated pools. For per-token cost we'll show the arithmetic: tokens per GPU-second, plus infra overhead (network, storage), plus overhead for prefix cache misses.
02:40 Ben Carter: Do you have a simple back-of-envelope formula we can use to sanity-check?
02:48 Maya Singh: Yes, we'll share the workbook: cost per token = (GPU_hour_rate / tokens_generated_per_hour) + infra_overhead + amortized_control_plane. For example, on an A100-like instance: if you get 10M tokens/hour, and the GPU rate is $5/hour -> $0.0005 per token base, add cache miss multiplier and infra overhead up to $0.0009 per token. But actual depends on batching and sequence length.
03:12 Priya Rao: What about peak and tail? We need to understand tail latencies under 95-99p during spikes.
03:20 Luis Ortega: We'll run p95/p99 measurements in the bench. Redwood also supports immediate fallback to smaller model variants when latency breaches SLO — that will be part of the rollout policy.
03:36 Jordan Park: Timeline: 1) Env & access + data samples (week 1), 2) Baseline local and Redwood hosted dry run (week 2), 3) Full benchmarks and quality evals (week 3-4), 4) Final econ report and recommendations (week 5-6). So 6 weeks end-to-end if artifacts and infra creds are timely.
03:58 Ben Carter: For private deployment (VPC) what are the cost differences? We expect higher infra ops but lower per-token raw cost once reserved capacity is used.
04:08 Maya Singh: Exactly — Dedicated/reserved capacity tends to lower unit GPU cost but has commit and management overhead. We'll include a section comparing Hosted-on-demand, Dedicated monthly reserved, and Private VPC (customer infra) with a rolling example for a 12-month amortization.
04:26 Sara Lopez: Can you also show the break-even point — at what steady-state request volume does dedicated become cheaper?
04:32 Jordan Park: We'll compute break-even volume and include sensitivity to cache hit-rate and average sequence length.
04:40 Priya Rao: On security/compliance, we need to confirm HIPAA data flow, KMS support, and audit bitrate — specifically, how long logs are retained and whether token-level content is stored.
04:55 Maya Singh: We'll attach the security brief; short answer: with Private you control the logs and KMS, hosted has configurable log retention and redaction but we'll run through the exact fields in the security doc.
05:09 Ben Carter: Bench questions: what are the inputs you'll need from us?
05:15 Jordan Park: 1) 14-day request traces and token histogram, 2) representative prompt+reference pairs for the 1k eval set, 3) desired cache hit simulations (if you have real prefix keys), 4) access constraints for VPC (if you want private run).
05:31 Ben Carter: We'll get the traces and prompt pairs. Expect them by Monday the 10th.
05:36 Priya Rao: On budgets — we can't exceed $30k/mo during POC and ideally would be under $20k. How do you enforce that?
05:45 Maya Singh: We can cap throughput, set hard daily spend limits in the POC config, and run simulated traffic to make sure the plan stays within budgets. We'll provide the cost workbook which shows best/worst case scenarios.
05:58 Jordan Park: A few gotchas we've seen: (a) embeddings workloads often have very high token counts during indexing, so even low per-token cost can add up, (b) caching helps a lot for fequent prefixes but you need to tune TTLs to avoid stale outputs, (c) using smaller variants for tail fallback can keep SLOs while saving cost but requires careful quality gating.
06:18 Priya Rao: Ok that aligns. For the quality gate, we need to know thresholds for acceptable regression — say no more than 2% drop on our metric and no catastrophic failures on clinical cases.
06:30 Maya Singh: We'll run the provided 1k eval and flag any samples that deviate beyond your metric threshold; we'll also run human spot checks on top 50 flagged items.
06:42 Sara Lopez: On reporting format — can you give us both a slide summary and the raw workbook?
06:47 Jordan Park: Yes slide summary + workbook + raw logs and scripts. We'll also produce a short appendix with model variant tradeoffs and recommended production configs (batching, cache policies, quantization level).
06:58 Priya Rao: Great. Anything else?
07:02 Ben Carter: One more: can we run a short dry-run with our existing model container to measure baseline token throughput? That will make the comparison apples-to-apples.
07:09 Luis Ortega: Yes we can run a baseline harness, Maya will share runner scripts.
07:15 Jordan Park: Cool. Recap of next steps: Jordan send runbook and pricing workbook by 11/07; NovaHealth send traces + eval set by 11/10; Maya to draft bench scripts by 11/12; kickoff week of 11/17.
07:33 Priya Rao: Thanks everyone, looking forward to it.
07:36 Jordan Park: Thanks, we'll follow up in email and slack.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors: "pri·a" sometimes rendered as "prior", "KV cache" as "K V cache", some acronyms lowercased. Natural pauses and filler words retained.
